A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same differential temporal-difference learning work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPO experiments on four continuous-control environments, including process-noise comparisons in Figure 2 and a diffusion-term ablation in Figure 3.

after.justification: v4 retains the original continuous-control experiments and learning curves in Section 6 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: Table 1 rescales the stated naive-dTD target and prediction by gamma: the prediction becomes gamma times V, changing the written residual normalization. The principal dTD formula, beta-dTD mixing rule and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. An implementation change or experimental rerun is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Hopper, HalfCheetah, Ant and Humanoid with process-noise coefficients 0.00, 0.01 and 0.05. Removing the diffusion ablation does not remove deterministic-environment coverage, which remains in Figure 2.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains TD, beta-naive-dTD and beta-dTD. However, v1's separate comparison against beta-dTD without the diffusion term, shown in Figure 3, is absent from v4.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same PPO framework, noise injection, environment time steps, reward and discount conversion, evaluation axes and DEHB tuning procedure. Tables 2 and 3 retain the same search spaces and selected hyperparameters after matching reordered environment columns.

E4.justification: v4 removes the entire diffusion-term ablation across all four deterministic environments, including Figure 3 and its discussion. This eliminates the dedicated test of whether the second-derivative component helps without process noise. The process-noise comparisons and naive-dTD comparison remain.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains identical shaded bands. Appendix B.3 retains the fixed-training-seed statement and simulator nondeterminism caveat. Neither version specifies run counts, defines the bands statistically, or adds confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 2's learning curves, shaded bands and reported tuned beta values are unchanged. v4 removes Figure 3's diffusion-ablation results and the finding that retaining diffusion improves performance in deterministic environments; no replacement results are provided.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 and the supporting appendix replace the sup-norm contraction proposition with an infinitesimal-generator formulation, a weak-solution existence lemma and exponential L2 stability of idealized continuous-time dynamics. New assumptions include reflecting boundaries, uniform ellipticity and coercivity. Appendix A.1 also develops the averaged-dynamics/value-function equivalence, replacing the earlier justification and separate viscosity-solution discussion.

C1.justification: v4's abstract explicitly claims exponential convergence of idealized continuous-time dynamics, and its conclusion replaces the earlier HJB-operator contraction claim with this differently scoped guarantee. The central model-free dTD contribution and empirical learning-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 acknowledges that the HJB operator is generally not a contraction and explicitly excludes neural function-approximation errors from its convergence analysis. It revises the justification for beta-dTD and discusses the applicability of reflecting boundaries and uniform ellipticity. It also removes the interpretation that diffusion compensates for finite-sample perturbations in deterministic environments.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 replaces the anonymous code-and-Docker access statement with a GitHub code link already present in the introduction, dropping explicit Docker-environment availability. This changes the access documentation without establishing that the resource itself was removed. Hardware, training times, pseudocode and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 removes Wiltzer et al. (2022), expands the contrast with stochastic-control approaches in Section 3.3.1, and removes the argument linking contraction directly to existing TD convergence analyses. Most related literature remains; the Jia and Zhou 2022a/2022b changes merely relabel the same works.

P1.justification: The background is substantially reorganized around model-free learning and the choice of policy-evaluation targets, with a new stochastic-control contrast subsection. Related-work prose is edited, theoretical exposition and the conclusion are rewritten, and Appendix A is reorganized. Author contact details and acknowledgements are also added.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is removed, while Figures 1 and 2 retain their graphical content. Table 1 is reformatted, Table 3 reorders environment columns, and figures and tables shift relative to surrounding text. The title and author block also change layout.

improvement.justification: v4 improves calibration and clarity by withdrawing v1's contraction argument, whose derivative-difference bound does not follow from its stated assumptions, and explicitly limiting the replacement analysis to idealized dynamics. The gain is tempered by removal of the diffusion ablation and a sign error in v4's Appendix A.3.1: integration by parts requires a positive sign for the term containing derivatives of D. The clearer theoretical scope supports a limited improvement, but the revised proof still needs correction.
